en.html:
Without a sound, Muramasa set off toward the forest. I watched her melt into the shadows and gave my mind to the problem.

Simple searching was out of the question. Already the situation was different from yesterday. That the enemy would sit in one place forever, such a thing could not happen.

And this forest is too big for searching without direction.

So a plan was required. Some method to smoke out the enemy hiding somewhere in this sea of trees...

Not easy. At present their whole purpose is to buy time. This much is nearly certain. Using Ichizo Sorimachi to work on GHQ and get Kanae removed, that is their only way out. No other door is open to them.

While Inspector Ootori remains in the village, the magistrate's people cannot make a move. Harm her and they lose GHQ, their lifeline. Once she is gone, they can do exactly as they like.

From the village's side, the clock is the same. If the magistrate is not removed while the inspector is present, there is no future. After she leaves, he recovers his power and resistance becomes difficult. And even if resistance succeeded, it would be an uprising: the village in rebellion against the shogunate.

Ruin, in other words. But right now Inspector Ootori will take the entire responsibility for removing him. Only now does the village have a chance to win.

My circumstances are different, but the conclusion is the same.

For us, now is the chance. For the magistrate's party, now is the time to lie low.

...This rule, the enemy must understand completely.

So how was I to pull him out of it...?

Sayo"Report accurately, Lieutenant Ootori. Your conduct follows the career of the the Lackland in being wholly incomprehensible. I cannot make head or tail of it. An explanation that makes sense, if you please."
Sayo"Oh? How strange. I thought I was being as plain and straightforward as the campaigns of the Lionheart. One sentence will explain the whole thing, you know?"
Sayo"Then give me the sentence."
Sayo"There was an evil magistrate, so I dealt with him."
Sayo"I am not familiar with Japanese jokes."
Sayo"Oh, that will never do, Lieutenant Colonel Cobden! A pillar of Civil Affairs, and the local customs you do not know? My poor abilities are at your service. Let us put that right."
Sayo"The neighbors have built a circle, I hear. Oh, Sir Cool! ...First the joke you must appreciate. Then we can proceed."
Sayo"............Very kind, but one lifetime will not suffice for that. I surrender. Now, shall I continue giving all my limited working hours to you alone?"
Sayo"Oh, look at me, keeping such a busy lieutenant colonel waiting. Most inconsiderate. Please accept my apologies. I shall take my leave, then. Until next time—"
Sayo"COMPLETE THE REPORT!"
Sayo"There was an evil magistrate—"
Sayo"Enough of the magistrate! From the beginning. So that I can understand."
Sayo"Once upon a time, in a certain place, an old man and an old woman were living. The old man went to the mountain to cut grass, and the old woman to the river to wash clothes..."
Sayo"What story is this?"
Sayo"This incident, from the beginning. With a little embellishment, naturally—why should the listener suffer boredom also? Just after this comes the extraordinary twist: from a peach, a warrior is born."

Sayo"...OK, OK. No thank you. If a proper report is beyond your abilities, I must make do. On the information already in my possession, I shall judge."
Sayo"Had you done that at the start, how nice it would have been. But the gentry are wonderful people. Every unnecessary step, they take it properly."
Sayo"Yes... even the physically or intellectually inferior I do not shun. Rather, I protect them. noblesse oblige, you understand. You ought to be grateful."
Sayo"From the bottom of my heart! To one physically and intellectually my superior, all my gratitude. By the way, Lieutenant Colonel, that chair which could not bear the weight—has it been repaired?"
Sayo"The chair that broke because of poor workmanship? Yes. I am quite comfortable now. Your concern is unnecessary. Let us talk about you instead."
Sayo"Oh, such words. Straight to the heart they go. Have you booked a room at the Peninsula for me?"
Sayo"Unfortunately I have not managed quite that much. Will you make do with the guardhouse?"
Sayo"An invitation from you, Lieutenant Colonel? How could I refuse? Only, there is a difficulty. The guardhouse is a paradise reserved for those who have committed a military blunder."
Sayo"Merely doing an inspector's duty, will I qualify?"
Sayo"Surely you have understood GHQ policy? Noninterference in the politics of the Rokuhara Shogunate. Your actions are a clear violation."
Sayo"Of course I have understood the policy. To secure the peace of Yamato's citizens, the shogunate is to be trusted with everything. That is the policy, no?"
